source.title_on_document: IdeaBlocks: Expressing and Reusing Divergent Intents for Graphic Design Exploration using Generative AI

supplement.where: Appendices A-D are included in this PDF on pp. 18-22. Separate supplementary material containing full pipeline prompts is cited on p. 8, Section 4.2, and p. 19, Appendix B.1; those prompts are not included in this PDF and no URL is supplied.
supplement.holds: Included appendices contain formative and evaluation participant tables (Tables 2 and 4), the thematic codebook (Table 3), image-generation pipeline details, the baseline screenshot, interview protocols, and example linkographs (Figure 10). Table 5 on p. 22 contains the CSI and NASA-TLX survey means, SDs and p-values. The separate, unread supplement contains the full prompts.

paper_design_summary: A counterbalanced within-person comparative study (Study 1, 12 people) compared IdeaBlocks with a free-prompt DALL-E 3 baseline plus ChatGPT during two 20-minute design-exploration rounds; random assignment of order is not stated. Outcomes included image and input-block counts, image-generation rates, maximum within-session CLIP distance, and linkography measures (PDF pp. 9-12, Sections 6-6.2.3). The paper also reports a qualitative formative study (7 people), model-pipeline validation (100 suggestions rated by 3 raters), and a descriptive three-day longitudinal study (6 people), with one participant shared between the comparative and longitudinal studies (PDF pp. 4, 9, 13 and 20).

arms.name: IdeaBlocks
arms.description: Canvas tool where divergent intent is entered as Exploration Blocks (property, direction keyword, typicality slider), with GPT-4o suggestions and block- and path-level reuse; images from DALL-E 3. Project-level reuse was disabled in this study.

arms.name: Baseline
arms.description: Same canvas interface; a free-form text prompt generates four DALL-E 3 images per block, reuse copies the preceding prompt; participants also had ChatGPT access.

participants.who: 12 people with a design background: six graduate design students, three final-year undergraduate design students, two working design-degree holders, and one graphic designer without a formal degree; recruited by online post
participants.quote: We recruited 12 participants (5 females; M=25, SD=1.71) through an online recruitment post. All had a design background through education or professional experience.
participants.locator: pp. 9-10, Section 6.1.1; N=12 also in the abstract, p. 1

ai_tool.name_model: IdeaBlocks (GPT-4o pipeline, DALL-E 3 images) vs baseline (DALL-E 3 via free-form prompt, plus ChatGPT)
ai_tool.how_used: Participants generated images to explore design concepts; the arms differ in how divergent intent is expressed and reused (structured blocks vs free-form prompts)

task.description: Generate diverse design concepts for one of two topics: a book-cover illustration for a detective novel set in a future city, or a mascot for a summer night urban film festival
task.duration: 20 minutes per round after a 10-minute tutorial; session about 1.5 hours

outcomes.name: Ideational fluency: number of generated images in the 20-minute session
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Number of images generated during each assisted 20-minute session. Figure 8 also presents image-generation rates in 4-minute segments with 95% confidence intervals; the text reports increasing rates with IdeaBlocks and no such acceleration in the baseline. This is a temporal variant of image-count fluency, shown in a figure; numerical rates and interval endpoints are not transcribed or estimated. PDF p. 11, Section 6.2.3 (Ideational Fluency); p. 12, Figure 8.

outcomes.name: Linkography: average link distance
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Computed from a separate linkograph for each participant’s session in each condition; nodes represent input blocks. Links capture parent-child connections, intent-reuse actions and explicit references to earlier ideas in think-aloud data. This measures the structure of a person’s idea development within a session, not diversity across people; nodes and links are not additional participants. PDF p. 11, Section 6.2.2; p. 21, Appendix D.1 and Figure 10.

ai_tool.how_used: Participants generated mascot concepts, verbalized their current intents and expectations, and assessed whether the generated results reflected their intent.

task.description: Explore diverse mascot designs for the participant’s company or department. studies.label: Pipeline evaluation: typicality ordering of model suggestions

assignment.what_was_assigned: Suggestions were randomly sampled from a generated candidate pool for human annotation; no people were assigned AI assistance.
assignment.quote: After that, we randomly selected 100 suggestions (60 text-based, 40 image-based) as a final evaluation set.
assignment.prereg_locator: No preregistration statement found in the complete document, including Appendices A-D (PDF pp. 1-22).

arms.name: IdeaBlocks suggestion pipeline
arms.description: Model-generated text- and image-based suggestions evaluated for alignment between pipeline typicality ordering and human judgments; no human-output comparison arm.

participants.who: Evaluation corpus of 100 model-generated suggestions (60 text-based, 40 image-based), randomly sampled from a pool of 400. Three raters with prior design experience supplied typicality judgments; these raters are not participants assigned AI assistance.
participants.quote: We recruited 3 raters with prior design experience

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4o suggestion pipeline with GloVe (text) and CLIP (image) typicality scoring
ai_tool.how_used: The pipeline generated candidate suggestions from five property-direction pairs drawn from the formative study; pipeline ordering was compared with averaged human typicality ratings (PDF p. 9, Section 4.2.1).

task.description: Human raters labeled the typicality of generated suggestions given an input property and direction. This validates the model pipeline; it is not a study of AI assistance to people creating outputs (PDF p. 9, Section 4.2.1).

outcomes.name: Typicality validation: alignment of pipeline ordering with human judgments
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Three design-experienced raters labeled 100 suggestions (60 text-based, 40 image-based); ratings were averaged. Krippendorff’s Alpha was 0.75 for text-based and 0.69 for image-based suggestions. Alignment with human annotations: text-based Pearson r=0.68 and Spearman rho=0.67; image-based Pearson r=0.59 and Spearman rho=0.58. These are validation correlations, not arm effects on human creativity. PDF p. 9, Section 4.2.1 (Pipeline Evaluation).

eligibility.reason: Study 1 analyzes 12 people, each using both AI configurations; the arm counts are repeated observations of the same people, not distinct samples (PDF pp. 9-10, Sections 6.1.1-6.1.3; p. 20, Table 4). The study states that topic and system order was counterbalanced but does not establish random assignment, so its design is coded other and criterion 1 remains unclear. Its image/block counts, within-session CLIP distance and linkography measures are computed from participant-created outputs (PDF pp. 10-12, Sections 6.1.4-6.2.3 and Table 1), meeting criterion 3, but its sample is below 50. The formative study has 7 people and the longitudinal study has 6, with no scored creativity/diversity comparison; the pipeline evaluation has 100 model suggestions and 3 raters, not people assigned assistance (PDF pp. 4, 9 and 13). P9/D3 is shared between Study 1 and Study 2 (PDF p. 20, Table 4 footnote); samples, raters and outputs are not pooled to meet the threshold. No randomized people study, AI-versus-human-output comparison, eligible observational contrast or synthesis is established; retain only in the screening report.

one_line_finding: In a within-subjects study of 12 designers, IdeaBlocks sessions produced more images (M=123.42 vs 58, p=0.0005) and a larger maximum CLIP cosine distance among a session's images (0.6384 vs 0.5675, p=0.0457) than a free-prompt DALL-E 3 baseline (p. 11, Table 1).
notes: The complete markdown conversion was read in chunks through Appendix D.2. Source passages and all retained or added numerical results were checked against extracted PDF text, including Table 1 and Appendices A-D. S1 denotes the comparative study, S2 the longitudinal study, S3 the formative study and S4 the model-pipeline evaluation. S4-O1 is recorded only to identify the validation dataset and its output count; question=none excludes it from the human-assistance questions. Formative intent assessments and longitudinal reuse logs/interviews do not supply scored creativity/diversity contrasts. Perceived creativity, CSI and NASA-TLX are self-reports, so they are not treated as independent output ratings (PDF pp. 10-14 and 22). The absence of a preregistration or explicit primary-outcome designation is coded not_stated. Appendix B.1 describes both the DALL-E 3 pipeline and a GPT-image-1 update (PDF pp. 18-19); Section 7 does not identify which image-model version was used in the longitudinal deployment.
